title: Describe the friction
intro: Most of us wait until we know exactly what to ask AI. Brian Casel of Builder Methods suggests the opposite: just say where it hurts, and let AI help you work out the fix. Copy this into ChatGPT, fill in the brackets, and send.
prompt:
I'm a real estate agent. Here's a part of my week that feels slow, confusing or keeps going wrong:
[describe it, for example: new leads from my website sit for a day or two before I call them back, and some go cold]

Don't jump to one answer. Ask me up to three questions to understand it, then give me two or three ways to fix it in plain words, simplest first. For each, say what AI could handle and what I should keep doing myself. Don't ask for client names or private details.
promptNote: What you'll get back: a few quick questions, then two or three fixes to pick from.

secondBrain.intro: Got a Second Brain from Signal-Edge Steps? Run this one inside your Second Brain project in the ChatGPT desktop app. Your AI checks your own notes for the same snag, then saves the fix and the prompt, so next time you just say "run Friction fix".
secondBrain.prompt:
Read the AGENTS.md rulebook in this folder first, then my About me notes and the last two weeks of Daily notes. If any are empty, carry on without them.
Here's a part of my week that feels slow, confusing or keeps going wrong:
[describe it]

Check my notes for other times this came up. Ask me up to three questions, then give me two or three fixes, simplest first. For each, say what you could take on using what's already in this folder, and what I should keep doing myself. Keep client names and details out.
When I pick a fix, save it as today's note in Daily notes. Then save this prompt in Scripts and templates as "Friction fix" and add it to My shortcuts in the AGENTS.md, so I can say "run Friction fix" next time. Show me each change before you save it.

homework: Run the prompt, then hit reply and tell me which fix you picked.
